summary: The run is at its budget limit and the record is complete, so this is a close rather than new work: all fourteen registered questions are answered, no necessary gaps or uncited executions remain, and the last premise I re-verified against the captured source — that startStopReplication registers replication state for every server in the latest configuration, nonvoters included — holds, so nothing needed correcting. Final state of the investigation: three execution-grounded findings, each with retained receipts, declared comparisons, witnesses and scoped conditions. The RestoreCommittedLogs startup replay blocks NewRaft through a blocking FSM-channel send issued before the FSM goroutine starts and before any handle is returned, from a window above 128 batches (8192 entries at the default batch size), confirmed at that boundary with the constructor's blocked stack and with the default snapshot settings in force. VerifyLeader counts acknowledgements from every registered peer, nonvoters included, against a quorum that counts only voters, so a leader whose only reachable peer is a nonvoter is confirmed; under per-node timers that confirmation outlived a competing leader's election in twenty of twenty trials and coincided with a commit index above the confirming leader's applied index in twelve of twelve, while uniform clusters kept the separation even at a one-millisecond margin, with the gate that produces the separation identified. AddVoter installs a Voter in one step against two published descriptions that promise staging, which can strand a single-voter cluster with no leader, no commits, and no in-band way back until the added server runs. Five suspicions were refuted with evidence rather than argument, one behaviour entry was corrected under its own id with its affected use answered, and several of my own earlier readings were narrowed by their own receipts — those narrowings are retained rather than tidied away.
